meetings.title: October 22, 2026 City Council Study Session
meetings.overview: The October 22, 2026 study session focused on two council priorities: bike security and wildfire resilience. Staff reported that bike theft fell 14% year-over-year and bike recovery rose 13%, with the team expecting to meet its 10% goals, and presented the Wildfire Ready 2030 framework along with roughly $1.85 million in proposed 2027 enhancements. No formal decisions were recorded; council members instead pressed staff on data gaps, e-bike theft, stronger wildfire hardening targets, a possible mandatory hardening ordinance, and evacuation planning.

topics.title: Bike Security and Theft Reduction Update
Enhancing Boulder's Wildfire Resilience

meetings.title: October 1, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting (Regular Meeting with Public Hearing on 2027 Budget)
meetings.overview: The October 1, 2026 Boulder City Council meeting centered on a public hearing on the 2027 recommended budget of about $552.6 million, which included wildfire funding, three new police lieutenants, and a proposed Spruce Pool operations reduction. Council adopted the 2027 budget ordinance 7-1 with Adams opposed, along with the mill levy, appropriation, and fee and tax ordinances, while proposals to hold or realign wildfire funds and to shift police funding toward behavioral health did not advance. The council also heard open comment on federal, housing, and development concerns, approved consent agenda items 3A through 3H unanimously, and unanimously directed staff to prepare a resolution supporting the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure.

meetings.title: September 24, 2026 City Council Study Session
meetings.overview: The September 24, 2026 study session covered police staffing, crime trends, and public safety integration, police oversight complaint data, municipal court cases involving unhoused defendants and young adults, and proposed updates to the sister cities program. It also touched on possible city uses of Boulder Valley School District properties, such as a police substation or training center. No formal votes were taken, but council generally supported a council committee to oversee sister city alliances, a possible cap on those alliances, and an escalating compliance process.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - September 17, 2026
meetings.overview: The September 17, 2026 Boulder City Council regular meeting heard public comment on the Panka Place vacation for Fraser Meadows senior housing, Boulder Valley School District school closures, the Glenn Huntington Bandshell seating redesign, CU South open space closure, and wildfire risk and density on University Hill. Council approved the consent agenda, with Shuhart and Spear voting no on items 4D and 4F and Benjamin voting no on 4F, and voted to call up the bandshell landmark alteration and a non-conforming duplex expansion at 969 10th Street, the latter 7-1. Council also unanimously adopted Ordinances 8765 and 8766, designating the Bird Stova House and the Hileman Bedell Stefanic Property as landmarks, and Ordinance 8770, repealing marijuana cultivation energy offset requirements.

meetings.title: September 10, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session - 2027 Recommended Budget
meetings.overview: The September 10, 2026 study session reviewed the City of Boulder's 2027 recommended budget, a $552.6 million plan that closes a $6.3 million general fund gap through reductions and new revenue, and the 2027 to 2032 capital program of $827.7 million. Council members pressed staff on the transparency of large projects like Alpine Balsam, how community priorities such as wildfire and public safety are itemized, restrictions on funds for Spruce Pool and senior discounts, and a proposal to shift about $2 million in climate funds to wildfire mitigation, which the mayor and others opposed without more analysis. No formal budget votes were taken; council members may submit amendments through the hotline by September 28, with first reading set for October 1 and adoption for October 15.

meetings.overview: The September 3, 2026 meeting covered public comment on the Frasier Meadows expansion, school closures, student rentals, and Spruce Pool funding, along with state housing laws and a set of routine items. Council approved the consent agenda, including the 2025-26 evaluations and salary adjustments for the city manager, city attorney, and municipal judge, with one dissent on that item, and approved the pedal cab licensing ordinance 7 to 0. Council also declined to call up the Frasier Meadows project because the motion failed for lack of a second, gave direction 5 to 3 to support the Boulder County commissioner expansion ballot measure, and directed informal outreach with restaurant owners and small businesses instead of forming a task force.

meetings.title: August 27, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session - Excel Energy Partnership Update and Wildfire Resilience
meetings.overview: At the August 27, 2026 Boulder City Council study session, Excel Energy reported on its 2020 franchise and energy partnership, including about 60% emissions reductions by the end of 2025 and wildfire mitigation work such as undergrounding three feeders and a two-phase transmission rebuild, while council pressed on outages, restoration communication, rates, and customer service. Staff then presented a draft home hardening hub, a project inventory of about 137 projects, and a draft risk index dividing the western wildland-urban interface into 12 sections, and council asked about contractors, renters, funding, and measurable 2030 targets. No formal decisions were made; staff committed to follow-up responses and a return to council in October.

meetings.title: August 6, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The August 6, 2026 Boulder City Council meeting centered on five potential November 2026 ballot measures, following open comment on topics including the shelter, Spruce Pool, and affordable housing HOA costs. Council referred the recreation and safety bond, the firefighter collective bargaining amendment, the residential vacancy excise tax (7-1, with Spear opposed), and the debt limit charter amendment to the ballot, while the downtown development authority failed 4-4 and staff was directed to scope further community engagement. Council also unanimously approved the remaining conditions and amendments to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update and passed consent agenda items 3A through 3C.

meetings.title: July 30, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Tip Offset Ordinance 8754 Second Reading and Public Hearing; Wildfire Resilience on Open Space Ballot Measure Direction)
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council's July 30, 2026 special meeting centered on a second reading and public hearing on Tip Offset Ordinance 8754, which would set a local tip offset for food and beverage workers, and on direction for a wildfire resilience measure on open space. After hearing from about 28 residents and industry groups, the council took no action to amend the tip offset, so the existing minimum wage schedule will proceed as scheduled. On wildfire resilience, the council opted against a ballot measure this year, chose to pursue an ordinance instead, and scheduled an executive session for legal advice before further action.

meetings.title: July 23, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Airport Funding and BVCP Public Hearings)
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council special meeting focused on airport funding and the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda, moved the BVCP adoption hearing to August 6, and heard staff financial scenarios, legal advice on FAA obligations, and dozens of public comments on the airport's future. After amendment, council voted 8-1 to continue airport operations, with council approval required for the next FAA grant that carries perpetuity obligations. Councilmember Wallik also announced his resignation at the end of the meeting.

meetings.title: June 25, 2026 - Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan major update deliberation, 2026 ballot measure polling and Fund Our Future engagement results)
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council special meeting focused on deliberations for the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan major update, where Council unanimously approved the update with its straw-poll-based amendments, conditions, and recommended changes, including adding wildfire integration language to policy 89. Council also gave non-binding direction on 2026 ballot measures, agreeing to pursue a tax increase for city facilities and operations, advancing a $400 million recreation and safety bond (eight votes) and a vacancy excise tax (seven votes) for further consideration. The meeting closed with a presentation of Fund Our Future engagement results, in which wildfire response and prevention ranked as the top priority, and a long-term financial strategy due in November 2026.

meetings.title: May 28, 2026 Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session
meetings.overview: The May 28, 2026 Boulder City Council special meeting and study session covered a consent item endorsing Councilmember Matt Benjamin's Colorado Municipal League Executive Board nomination, which passed 8 to 0 with Benjamin recused, and unanimous adoption of Ordinance 8749, granting possible eminent domain authority for the $12 million Arapahoe Avenue safety project. The council also voted to hold a public hearing on the future of airport land use and directed staff to return with two options and legal research, while a study session on a proposed Downtown Development Authority plan drew concerns about general fund impacts, parking governance, and equity for University Hill, though members generally supported moving forward. Staff now seeks direction on the plan's feedback, financing structure, and November 2026 ballot measures.

meetings.overview: The May 14, 2026 Boulder City Council study session focused on the city's financial outlook, including lowered sales and property tax forecasts, a $6.5 million 2027 general fund shortfall, the 2027 budget calendar, and facilities funding needs. meetings.overview: The April 23, 2026 Boulder City Council study session focused on the future of the Boulder Municipal Airport and on power resilience amid rising public safety power shutoffs. On power resilience, council voiced support for the phased community engagement approach and confirmed alignment with it after questioning accountability, timelines, and relocation considerations.

meetings.overview: At its March 5, 2026 regular meeting, the Boulder City Council heard public comment on the Flock Safety license-plate-reader contract and the South Boulder Recreation Center, received updates on the Frontier Avenue redevelopment and the city's affordable housing program, and took action on several agenda items. The council unanimously approved the consent agenda and the 2026 board and commission appointments, and it directed staff to revise the Area Three guidance so that housing there is not limited to middle-income ownership. No decisions were made on the Flock contract or the recreation center, which staff will address further in future work, including an April 9 study session on facilities funding.

meetings.title: February 19, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting (Boulder City Council)
meetings.overview: The February 19, 2026 Boulder City Council regular meeting opened with public comment on the future of the South Boulder Rec Center pool and gym, where many residents and swim team members urged the council to keep the facilities, though staff said no decisions have been made and rec center discussions are planned for spring study sessions. The council also approved consent agenda items 3A and 3B, adopted Resolution 1370, Ordinance 8734, and a Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan land use change to annex about 24 acres at 5399 Kowani Drive and 5697 South Boulder Road, and gave non-binding feedback on a concept to redevelop the Pearl Street storage site with about 281 apartments. Other public comments covered topics such as trail safety, property taxes, and climate resilience, and staff committed to follow up on several of them.

meetings.title: February 12, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council's February 12, 2026 special meeting centered on the Area 3 Planning Reserve, where council voted 7-2 to find six identified community needs, including housing, fire storage, and parkland, a high enough priority to warrant further consideration of a service area expansion plan and directed staff to bring back a guiding resolution. Council also unanimously approved the consent agenda after removing item 6A, and it declined to reconsider five community change requests that Boulder County commissioners had asked it to revisit. The remaining items were informational: a municipal court update on 2025 caseloads and legal changes to monitor, and a preview of 2026 council engagement options, where members favored chats and forums and asked staff to estimate capacity for each method.

meetings.title: February 5, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.overview: The February 5, 2026 regular council meeting covered public concerns over the South Boulder Recreation Center, a Black History Month declaration, a rezoning of 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue to MU-4, the 2026 policy statement on regional, state, and federal issues, House Bill 26-1010 (the HOME Act), and council priorities and process improvements. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda and both rezoning ordinances, and it directed staff to pursue several amendments to House Bill 26-1010 after a straw poll. Staff said recreation center decisions would return to council in March and May, while the policy statement additions and retreat priorities were discussed without a formal vote recorded.

meetings.title: January 22, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The January 22, 2026 special meeting covered the consent agenda, a purchasing code update, community change requests for the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, a proposed metro district policy framework, and a regional homelessness appointment, along with a Holocaust Remembrance Day declaration. Council unanimously passed consent items 3A through 3G, adopted Ordinance 8731 to modernize the city's purchasing procedures, and approved an amended list of comprehensive plan change requests that removed a Sue Drive request and added wildfire mitigation and agricultural water use requests. No final action was taken on the metro district framework, which staff will bring back in April with a regulating ordinance, and the regional homelessness working group appointment was deferred to a later consent item, with Tina volunteering as alternate.

meetings.title: January 8, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
meetings.overview: The January 8, 2026 special meeting covered the city's response to the December power shutoff and windstorm, which left about 60 percent of the community without power, along with a long public comment period and a series of consent, zoning, and district board items. Council approved the Sundance Film Festival governing agreement for 2027 through 2036, with parking revenue sharing at a 50/50 split, and adopted the 915 Fifth Street annexation with initial Residential Estate zoning. It also passed the wildfire hardening and water-wise landscaping ordinance on second reading with amendments, while failing a 4-5 vote to call up the five-story Arapahoe Avenue project.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - October 12, 2023
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council study session opened with Council Member Tara Winer's remarks on the October 7 Hamas attacks in southern Israel and Boulder's ties to its sister city, Ramat Hanegev. The council generally supported continuing the Camp shiaka parking and shuttle program and studying direct transit access, while raising concerns about fairness to Boulder residents and higher parking costs. It also unanimously agreed to take a support position on Boulder County Ballot Measure 1A, a 0.5% open space sales tax extension, with staff asked to place the item on the next business meeting's consent agenda, and it gave staff feedback on East Boulder form-based code, with draft recommendations to follow in a few months.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - Thursday October 5, 2023
meetings.overview: The October 5, 2023 Boulder City Council meeting opened with public comment on reservoir fees, pollinator gardens, street safety, policing, and homelessness, followed by proclamations and several agenda items. Council annexed and zoned 3033 Third Street RL-1, adopted Ordinances 8595 through 8598 for the 2024 budget with amended transportation and general fund appropriations, and passed consent agenda items 3A through 3G, with the mayor pro tem opposing 3G. By majority vote, council also directed staff to develop a pilot safe outdoor space for about 25 people and to return with cost and location details, while staff recommended expanding prairie dog removal after a three-year program review.

meetings.overview: The September 28, 2023 Boulder City Council study session covered Municipal Court operations, the Police Department's crime trends and recent incidents, and homelessness programs, including alternative sheltering options. Judge Khan and staff explained court procedures, jail and bond constraints, and the Community Court model, while Chief Harold reported rising violent and drug-related crime and the Police Department's community engagement efforts. No formal votes were taken, but council members voiced frustration with repeat offenders and differing views on safe outdoor spaces versus indoor shelter beds, and they directed staff to bring a formal item back, likely tied to budget discussions.

meetings.overview: At its September 21, 2023 regular meeting, the Boulder City Council presented Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day declarations, heard public comment on topics including a library building, a Central Park homeless camping incident, and local housing, and approved its consent agenda. meetings.title: September 14, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session: Library District IGA Direction and 2024 Recommended Budget Discussion
meetings.overview: The September 14, 2023 Boulder City Council study session covered the separation of the municipal library into a new Library District, including trustee appointments and the future of city-owned library buildings, along with a review of the $514.8 million 2024 recommended budget. Council directed staff to continue a hybrid trustee appointment process with a three-year check-in and to explore long-term building leases with five-year district termination options, and straw polls favored leasing over conveying the library properties. No budget decisions were made; council members raised concerns about behavioral health, housing, and street maintenance, and they were asked to submit proposed changes by September 25 ahead of the October 5 first reading.

meetings.overview: The September 7, 2023 Boulder City Council regular meeting opened with announcements, a unanimous vote to move the library district agreement to a September 14 study session, and commemorative declarations, followed by public comment on topics ranging from airport closure to police accountability. meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council study session covered community broadband, the airport community conversation, and minimum wage. Council generally leaned toward a backbone lease option for broadband, which carries about $218 million in build costs and a roughly $14 million annual subsidy, while the airport discussion on noise, leaded fuel, and airspace reached no decision. On minimum wage, council gave a split direction to stay with its 2025 timeline rather than join Boulder County's faster 2024 schedule.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - Thursday August 17 2023
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council meeting on August 17, 2023 covered a clean 2022 audit report, public comment urging a higher local minimum wage, and several ballot and housing measures. Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3I, adopted ordinances 8586 and 8587, and approved a 50-50 arts and general fund sales tax compromise (ordinance 8591) as an emergency measure so it could reach the November ballot, after rejecting a 100 percent arts option. Council also adopted ordinance 8585 by a 6-3 vote, raising the citywide unrelated-person occupancy limit to five after a public hearing with dozens of speakers.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session - August 10, 2023
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council special meeting and study session covered board appointments, revitalization of the University Hill commercial district, and a proposed affordable commercial pilot program. Council made five appointments to the Environmental Advisory Board, Landmarks Board, Open Space Board of Trustees, and University Hill Commercial Area Management Commission, approving them unanimously after a finalist process. On University Hill, council generally backed staff's plan to prioritize district-wide strategies before redeveloping the 14th Street parking lot and asked staff to explore code changes, while on the affordable commercial pilot it supported further exploration but raised questions about cost, sustainability, and selection criteria.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - August 3, 2023
meetings.overview: The August 3, 2023 Boulder City Council meeting covered a pollinator declaration, extensive public comment on homelessness, housing, and development, and several land-use, ballot, and homeless-services items. Council approved the consent agenda (with Weiner, Yates, and Mayor Pro Tem Walling opposed to item 3B), unanimously adopted Ordinance 8580 designating the Powers House at 830 14th Street as a landmark, and selected a 50/50 split for the proposed 0.15 percent sales tax extension, with three related ballot ordinances held for final action on August 17. Council also directed staff to add safe outdoor spaces and micro communities to the scope of the external homeless services evaluation, and staff gave an update on the 311 Mapleton land dedication, which is set to close the following week.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Study Session - July 27, 2023 (Police Oversight Ordinance Update; Use Table and Standards Update - Neighborhood Centers)
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council study session on July 27, 2023, covered two topics: a preliminary review of revisions to the city's police oversight ordinance, including panel scope, selection, onboarding, and training, and the third module of the use table update for neighborhood center business and mixed-use zones. Council members supported the police oversight work and asked for comparisons with other cities, and they broadly backed streamlining restaurant approvals and expanding small-business uses while debating ground-floor residential uses, drive-throughs and gas stations, and clubs and hostels. No formal decisions were made, and the police oversight recommendations are expected in the fall, while the neighborhood center ordinance is slated for October after community input closes July 31 and planning board review in August.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - July 20, 2023
meetings.overview: The July 20, 2023 Boulder City Council regular meeting opened with public participation, where residents urged the council to keep smoke-free air laws and raised concerns about minimum wage, airport noise, lead exposure, and homelessness. The council then discussed whether to opt into state law allowing marijuana hospitality establishments, weighing workload, consultant costs, and whether a future council should decide, and most members preferred not to begin engagement now. The meeting also covered Boulder Creek safety after recent drownings, including county flow thresholds, planned throw line stations, signage, expanded swim lessons, and possible changes to rescue protocols and youth outreach.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting - July 13, 2023
meetings.overview: The July 13, 2023 special meeting covered a Parks and Recreation Month declaration, which council adopted, and the consent agenda, which it approved unanimously. Council also held comment-only reviews of the New Vista High School site development plan and a North Boulder mixed-use concept at 4401 Broadway that includes a new museum, and it requested a referral to the Tax Advisory Board on the latter. On the sales tax ballot question, council directed staff to prepare a 50/50 split alternative between the general fund and arts and to conduct further outreach, while most members chose to wait until 2024 rather than extend midterm recruitment for boards and commissions.

meetings.title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session - June 20, 2023
meetings.overview: The Boulder City Council's June 20, 2023 special meeting and study session covered a wide range of items, including a recognition of Judge Linda Cook's two decades of service, a rezoning of 5405 Spine Road, and a briefing on the municipal court's community navigation program. Council adopted a consent agenda that included an ordinance imposing an emergency moratorium on police oversight panel case intake, with council members Wallach and Yates voting against it, and unanimously adopted the Spine Road rezoning ordinance on second reading. Discussion also addressed the county clerk's election review and ranked choice voting for mayor, potential November ballot measures, and the 2024 energy code, where a straw poll showed majority support for moving toward 100 percent electrification of new construction.
